literal: In the sixth month, day Wuxu, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Chariot.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on Wuxu, Venus appeared in broad daylight within the Chariot asterism (Zhěn).

literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
idiomatic: The same omen gloss was applied as before.

literal: The Chariot is the field allotment of Chu.
idiomatic: Zhěn marks Chu’s celestial field.

literal: On day Renzi, the moon transgressed the Net.
idiomatic: On renzi the Moon crossed the Net (Bi) asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is border troops."
idiomatic: The omen-text reads: "Foretells frontier warfare."

literal: In the seventh month, day Xinsi, Mars transgressed the Celestial River.
idiomatic: In the seventh month, on xinsi, Mars drew near the Celestial River.

literal: The prognostication states: "Fords and ferries are blocked."
idiomatic: The gloss warns of blocked rivers and cut supply lines.

literal: In the eleventh month, Jupiter transgressed the Chamber.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Jupiter crossed the House (Fang) mansion.

literal: The prognostication states: "Yu Province will have calamity."
idiomatic: The text points to disaster in the Yu region.

literal: In that year’s fifth month, Fu Jian killed Fu Sheng and established himself.
idiomatic: That May, Fu Jian slew Fu Sheng and took the throne.

literal: In the twelfth month, Murong Jun entered and encamped at Ye.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Jun marched in and garrisoned Ye.

literal: In the eighth month of the second year, Inspector of Yu Province Xie Yi died.
idiomatic: In the second year’s eighth month, Yu provincial inspector Xie Yi passed away.

literal: In the second year, second month, day Xinmao, Saturn transgressed the great star of the Coachman.
idiomatic: On xinmao in the second month of the second year, Saturn crossed the chief star of Xuanyuan.

literal: The prognostication states: "The ruler finds it ominous."
idiomatic: The omen warns the sovereign of ill portent.

literal: On day Jiawu, the moon transgressed the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: On jiawu the Moon trespassed against the Eastern Well.

literal: In the sixth month, day Xinyou, the moon transgressed the Chamber.
idiomatic: On xinyou in the sixth month the Moon crossed the House mansion.

literal: In the tenth month, day Jiwei, the Great White transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiwei, Venus closed on the Weeping star.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be great weeping."
idiomatic: The gloss foretells widespread mourning and lamentation.

literal: In the third year, first month, day Renchen, Mars transgressed the Bolt-and-Lock star.
idiomatic: On renchen in the first month of the third year, Mars crossed the Gate-bolt stars.

literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "The ruler will be anxious."
idiomatic: The commentary gloss reads: "The throne faces worry."

literal: In the third month, day Yiyou, Mars retrograded and transgressed the Hook-and-Hasp.
idiomatic: On yiyou in the third month Mars moved retrograde against the Hook-and-Hasp.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "The king finds it ominous."
idiomatic: The omen-text says the ruler should dread the sign.

literal: In the sixth month, the Great White transgressed the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Venus crossed the Eastern Well.

literal: In the seventh month, day Yiyou, Mars transgressed the Celestial River.
idiomatic: On yiyou in the seventh month Mars again neared the Celestial River.

literal: On day Bingxu, the Great White transgressed the Ghost Cart.
idiomatic: On bingxu Venus crossed the Ghost asterism (Yuguǐ).

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Every cited gloss matched the entries above.

literal: On day Wuzi, the moon transgressed the central great star of the Oxherd.
idiomatic: On wuzi the Moon crossed the central bright star of the Oxherd.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Oxherd is Heaven’s general."
idiomatic: The text identifies the Oxherd as the celestial commander’s seat.

literal: Transgressing the central great star means a general will die.
idiomatic: A strike on its central star portends a field marshal’s death.

literal: In the eighth month, day Dingwei, the Great White transgressed the great star of the Coachman.
idiomatic: On dingwei in the eighth month Venus crossed Xuanyuan’s chief star.

literal: On day Jiazi, the moon transgressed the great star of the Net.
idiomatic: On jiazi the Moon drew near the chief star of the Net.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is border troops."
idiomatic: Again the gloss reads: "Border warfare."

literal: One gloss says: The lower transgresses the upper.
idiomatic: Another line adds: subordinates rise against superiors.

literal: In the tenth month of the third year, Zhuge Hui’s river fleet entered the He and was defeated.
idiomatic: That October Zhuge Hui’s flotilla pushed up the Yellow River and met disaster.

literal: Inspector of Yu Province Xie Wan entered Ying; the host collapsed and returned; Wan was stripped of name.
idiomatic: Yu inspector Xie Wan marched into Yingzhou, his army routed; he returned in shame and lost his rank.

literal: In the eleventh month, the Minister of Education and Prince of Kuaiji, because the two commands of Xi Tan and Xie Wan had been defeated, submitted asking to degrade himself three ranks.
idiomatic: In November the Prince of Kuaiji, serving as Minister of Education, cited Xi Tan and Xie Wan’s twin defeats and memorialized for a three-grade self-demotion.

literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Murong Jun died; his son Wei succeeded him.
idiomatic: First month of the fourth year: Murong Jun died and his son Murong Wei inherited rule.

literal: Murong Ke killed his Director of the Secretariat Yang Wu and others.
idiomatic: Murong Ke executed Grand Secretary Yang Wu and associates.

literal: In the fourth year, first month, day Yihai, the moon transgressed the central great star of the Oxherd.
idiomatic: On yihai in the first month of the fourth year the Moon crossed the Oxherd’s central star.

literal: In the sixth month, day Xinhai, Mercury transgressed the Coachman.
idiomatic: On xinhai in the sixth month Mercury crossed Xuanyuan.

literal: The prognostication states: "The queen consort will be anxious."
idiomatic: The gloss warns of trouble for the empress.

literal: On day Jiwei, the Great White entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s right Censor Gate and exited by the Portal Gate.
idiomatic: On jiwei Venus slipped into the Supreme Palace through the right rear gate and left by the front portal.

literal: The prognostication states: "Nobles lose their power."
idiomatic: It portends great families stripped of influence.

literal: One gloss says: "There will be arms."
idiomatic: Another line adds armed conflict.

literal: It also says: "Exiting the Portal Gate means ministers are not ministerial."
idiomatic: A further gloss says leaving the Portal Gate marks ministers turning disloyal.

literal: In the eighth month, day Wushen, the Great White transgressed the Root.
idiomatic: On wushen in the eighth month Venus crossed the Root (Dǐ) stars.

literal: The prognostication states: "The state will have grief."
idiomatic: The realm faces mourning and worry.

literal: On day Bingchen, Mars transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s western bastion and the star of the senior commander.
idiomatic: On bingchen Mars neared the western rampart’s senior commander star in the enclosure.

literal: In the ninth month, day Renwu, the Great White entered the mouth of the Southern Dipper and transgressed its fourth star.
idiomatic: On renwu in the ninth month Venus entered the Dipper’s mouth and struck its fourth star.

literal: The prognostication states: "There is mourning; there is amnesty; the realm receives noble ranks and stipends."
idiomatic: It foretells funerals, a general pardon, and ennoblements across the land.

literal: In the twelfth month, day Jiayin, Mars transgressed the Chamber.
idiomatic: On jiayin in the twelfth month Mars crossed the House mansion.

literal: On day Bingyin, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: On bingyin Venus shone in daylight.

literal: On day Gengyin, the moon transgressed the Bolt-and-Lock; the prognostication states: "The ruler finds it ominous."
idiomatic: On gengyin the Moon crossed the Gate-bolt; the gloss warns the sovereign of dread.

literal: In the fifth year, first month, day Yisi, Saturn retrograded and transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: On yisi in the first month of the fifth year Saturn moved retrograde into the Supreme Palace.

literal: In the fifth month, day Renyin, the moon transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: On renyin in the fifth month the Moon crossed the enclosure.

literal: On day Gengxu, the moon transgressed the Establishment stars.
idiomatic: On gengxu the Moon trespassed against the Establishment asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "Great ministers plot one another."
idiomatic: High officials are set to intrigue against each other.

literal: At this time Yin Hao’s campaign collapsed and he ended in banishment.
idiomatic: That season Yin Hao’s army was routed and he was eventually removed to the margins.

literal: In that month, day Xinhai, the moon transgressed the Oxherd station.
idiomatic: That same month, on xinhai, the Moon crossed the Oxherd lodge.

literal: The prognostication states: "The state will have grief."
idiomatic: Again the gloss speaks of national mourning.

literal: In the sixth month, day Guihai, the moon transgressed the northeast star of the Root.
idiomatic: On guihai in the sixth month the Moon covered the Root’s northeast star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The grand general will answer for it."
idiomatic: A commander-in-chief will bear the brunt.

literal: In the fifth year, first month, North-of-the-River General Xi Tan died.
idiomatic: First month of the fifth year: North-of-the-River general Xi Tan passed away.

literal: In the fifth month the emperor died; Emperor Ai ascended; a great amnesty was proclaimed; noble ranks were granted; Empress Chu lost her influence.
idiomatic: In May the sovereign died, Emperor Ai succeeded, a sweeping pardon was issued, titles were handed out, and Empress Chu was sidelined.

literal: In the seventh month, Murong Ke attacked Inspector of Ji Province Lu Hu at Yewang; Hu fled to Xingyang.
idiomatic: In July Murong Ke besieged Ji inspector Lu Hu at Yewang, who bolted toward Xingyang.

literal: At this time Huan Wen, with a great host halted at Wan, heard of Hu’s defeat and withdrew.
idiomatic: Huan Wen had massed troops at Wan; learning of Lu Hu’s rout, he pulled back.

literal: In the fifth year, sixth month, day Guiyou, the moon covered the northeast star of the Root.
idiomatic: On guiyou in the fifth year’s sixth month the Moon occulted the Root’s northeast star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The grand general will answer for it."
idiomatic: The omen again targets the commander-in-chief.

literal: On day Yiyou in the ninth month, the moon covered the Net.
idiomatic: On yiyou in the ninth month the Moon occulted the Net.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be border troops."
idiomatic: Foretells frontier armies in motion.

literal: On day Dingwei in the tenth month, the moon transgressed the great star of the Net.
idiomatic: On dingwei in the tenth month the Moon crossed the Net’s chief star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The lower transgresses the upper."
idiomatic: Subordinates challenge their superiors.

literal: It also says: "There will be border troops."
idiomatic: Another line repeats a border-war warning.

literal: In the eighth month, Fan Wang was dismissed.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Fan Wang was cashiered.

literal: In the first year of Longhe, Murong Wei sent a general to raid Heyin.
idiomatic: Longhe year one: Murong Wei dispatched troops to strike Heyin.

literal: In Emperor Ai’s third Xingning year, seventh month, day Gengxu, the moon transgressed the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: Third Xingning year of Emperor Ai, seventh month, gengxu: the Moon crossed the Dipper.

literal: The prognostication states: "The queen consort will be anxious."
idiomatic: The empress faces ill portent.

literal: Jupiter transgressed the Ghost Cart.
idiomatic: Jupiter crossed the Ghost asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "The ruler will be anxious."
idiomatic: The sovereign should brace for trouble.

literal: In the tenth month, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Neck.
idiomatic: In the tenth month Venus appeared by day in the Neck (Kang).

literal: The prognostication states: "The Neck is the court; there will be arms and mourning; ministers will be strong."
idiomatic: Kang marks the court: expect war, funerals, and overbearing ministers.

literal: In the next year’s fifth month, Empress Yu died.
idiomatic: The following May Empress Yu passed away.

literal: In the first month of Emperor Fei’s second Taihe year, the Great White entered the Hairy Head.
idiomatic: First month of Taihe two under the deposed emperor: Venus entered the Pleiades lodge.

literal: In the fifth year, Murong Wei was destroyed by Fu Jian, who also held Si, Ji, You, and Bing provinces.
idiomatic: By the fifth year Murong Wei had fallen to Fu Jian, who controlled Si, Ji, You, and Bing.

literal: In the intercalary month of the sixth year, Mars guarded the Portal Gate of the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: The sixth year’s leap month saw Mars station at the enclosure’s Portal Gate.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven loses the state."
idiomatic: The gloss reads: the dynasty is lost.

literal: It also says: "Feudal lords and the Three Dukes plot against their ruler."
idiomatic: Another line warns that regional lords and chief ministers scheme against the throne.

literal: One gloss says: "There will be decapitated ministers."
idiomatic: A variant adds executions among senior officials.

literal: On day Xinmao, the moon transgressed the great star of the Heart.
idiomatic: On xinmao the Moon crossed Antares in the Heart.

literal: The prognostication states: "The king finds it ominous."
idiomatic: The sovereign should dread the sign.

literal: In the eleventh month, Huan Wen deposed the emperor and also memorialized to execute the Prince of Wuling; Emperor Jianwen forbade it, so Wen banished him to Xin’an; all were responses to strong ministers.
idiomatic: That November Huan Wen dethroned the sovereign and sought the Prince of Wuling’s death; Emperor Jianwen refused, so Wen banished the prince to Xin’an—classic signs of ministerial dominance.

literal: In Emperor Jianwen’s first Xian’an year, twelfth month, day Xinmao, Mars retrograded into the Supreme Palace Enclosure; in the third month of the second year it still had not withdrawn.
idiomatic: Xian’an one, twelfth month, xinmao: Mars moved retrograde into the Supreme Palace and remained through the third month of year two.

literal: The prognostication states: "The state is not secure; there is grief."
idiomatic: The realm stands unsettled under looming sorrow.

literal: At this time the emperor faced coercion from Huan Wen.
idiomatic: The court lived under Huan Wen’s intimidation.

literal: In the second year, fifth month, day Dingwei, the Great White transgressed the Celestial Pass.
idiomatic: On dingwei in the fifth month of the second year Venus crossed the Celestial Pass.

literal: The prognostication states: "Arms will arise."
idiomatic: The gloss reads: "Warfare will break out."

literal: Jupiter’s color and form were like the Great White’s.
idiomatic: Observers reported Jupiter’s hue and brilliance matching Venus.

literal: The prognostication states: "If advance and retreat match the measure, treachery ceases;
idiomatic: Another gloss reads: "When motion keeps proper measure, villainy subsides;"

literal: if color changes and motion is disorderly, the ruler will have no blessing."
idiomatic: but shifting color and erratic motion leave the sovereign without fortune."

literal: Jupiter in midsummer ought to be small and dim; this was its losing normality.
idiomatic: At midsummer Jupiter should appear faint and small—its bright, Venus-like show was plainly abnormal.
